rationale: C22 is a compelling direct template. Both letters designate a U.S. officer as a NATO supreme allied commander, anticipate a Standing Group directive defining the commander's authority, assign operational command of specified U.S. forces to the extent necessary for the mission, authorize a staff of military and civilian personnel in necessary numbers and grades, and send copies to the Secretaries of State and Defense for guidance. The later letter condenses and adapts this same sequence from the European command to the Atlantic command. C10 has some related allied-command machinery but lacks the distinctive language and sequence; C06 shares only generic letter-closing notification language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The North Atlantic Treaty Nations have agreed that a Supreme Allied Commander, Atlantic, should now be appointed and have requested that I designate a United States officer. I have designated you
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The North Atlantic Treaty Nations have agreed on the defense organization for Europe and at their request I have designated you as Supreme Allied Commander, Europe.
shared_material.explanation: Both open by citing agreement among the North Atlantic Treaty nations and their request for presidential designation of a U.S. supreme allied commander.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am informed that the Standing Group of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization will issue a directive to you concerning your responsibilities and authority as the Supreme Allied Commander, Atlantic.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I understand that the Standing Group of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization will shortly issue a directive to you concerning your responsibility and authority as the Supreme Allied Commander, Europe.
shared_material.explanation: This is highly distinctive, nearly verbatim language, altered chiefly for command title and minor tense or number changes.

shared_material.child_excerpt: You are hereby assigned operational command, of the United States Armed forces assigned to the U.S. Atlantic Command, to the extent necessary for the accomplishment of your mission.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You are hereby assigned operational command, to the extent necessary for the accomplishment of your mission, of the U.S. Army Forces, Europe; U.S. Air Forces, Europe; and the U.S. Naval Forces, Eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean.
shared_material.explanation: The same operative grant assigns operational command of the relevant U.S. forces, using the identical mission-limiting formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: You are hereby authorized to use officers and enlisted personnel of the U.S. Armed forces and civilian employees of the U.S. Government, on your staff as you consider appropriate in numbers and grades as necessary.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You are authorized to have officers and enlisted personnel of the U.S. Armed Forces, as well as civilian employees of the Departments of the Army, Navy and Air Force, for your Staff in such numbers and grades as you consider necessary.
shared_material.explanation: The staff authorization repeats the same categories of personnel and the distinctive discretion over their numbers and grades.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am sending copies of this letter to the Secretary of State and to the Secretary of Defense for their guidance.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am sending a copy of this letter to the Secretary of State for his guidance and a copy to the Secretary of Defense for his guidance and necessary action by the Department of Defense.
shared_material.explanation: The later letter preserves the same concluding distribution to the same two cabinet officers for guidance.
